Here’s what was implemented:

### 1. **Newest messages first** (`conversation_detail_panel.tsx`)

Merged messages are sorted by creation time using ISO strings (chronological when compared as strings):

```133:136:apps/frontend-pt1-extranet-onboarding/src/panels/conversation_detail_panel.tsx
  const messages = useMemo(() => {
    const combined = [...baseMessages, ...optimisticMessages];
    return combined.toSorted((a, b) => b.atIso.localeCompare(a.atIso));
  }, [baseMessages, optimisticMessages]);
```

`toSorted` is fine here because the app tsconfig includes **`ES2023`**.

### 2. **No chat-style auto-scroll on the email thread** (`PortalEmailThreadWindow.tsx`)

`ChatList` was removed from this component. That wrapper used `useChatAutoScroll`, which:

- Scrolls to the bottom on mount  
- Keeps pinning to the bottom when the DOM updates (`MutationObserver`)

That behavior stays on **`PortalChatWindow`** and Storybook demos that still import `ChatList`.

The thread is now a normal **`flex … min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto`** region with the same **`role="log"`**, **`aria-live="polite"`**, and **`aria-label`**, plus your existing **`scrollAreaClassName`**. Scroll position stays where the user left it when messages change.

---

**UX note:** “Most recent first” means the **top** of the list is the latest message when the panel opens (scroll starts at `0`). If you’d rather newest at the bottom with **no** auto-scroll, say so and we can switch sort order without bringing back auto-scroll.

content.text:
Here’s what was added and how it fits together.

### Thread cards (`PortalEmailThreadWindow`)
- Markdown **preview uses a max height** (default **12 rem**, overridable with `messageBodyPreviewMaxRem`).
- When content is taller than that, the bottom gets a **`from-card` gradient fade** so it’s obvious more text exists.
- If **`onOpenMessageDetail`** is set and the body is clipped, a link-style button appears: **«Volledig bericht bekijken»**.
- Attachments stay **below** the preview so they stay usable without opening the detail panel.

### Full message in a stacked panel (PT1 app)
- New panel type **`conversationMessageDetail`** (`CONVERSATION_MESSAGE_DETAIL_PANEL_TYPE` in [`conversation-panel-config.ts`](apps/frontend-pt1-extranet-onboarding/src/panels/conversation-panel-config.ts)), registered in [`panelRegistry.ts`](apps/frontend-pt1-extranet-onboarding/src/panels/panelRegistry.ts).
- [`conversation_detail_panel.tsx`](apps/frontend-pt1-extranet-onboarding/src/panels/conversation_detail_panel.tsx) publishes the sorted thread (including optimistic rows) via [`conversation-thread-messages-cache.ts`](apps/frontend-pt1-extranet-onboarding/src/panels/conversation-thread-messages-cache.ts) and calls **`openPanel(..., { suite, scenario, messageId })`** when the user requests the full message.
- [`conversation_message_detail_panel.tsx`](apps/frontend-pt1-extranet-onboarding/src/panels/conversation_message_detail_panel.tsx) reads that snapshot (fallback: sorted mock-only list from [`conversation-portal-email-messages.ts`](apps/frontend-pt1-extranet-onboarding/src/features/conversations/conversation-portal-email-messages.ts)).
- Footer nav: **«Nieuwer»** moves to a **more recent** message (up the newest-first list), **«Ouder»** to an **older** one.

### Minimal full-message layout (ui-lib)
- New [`PortalEmailMessageDetailBody`](packages/ui-lib/src/custom-components/Chat/portal-email-message-detail-body.tsx): sender, formatted time (long nl-BE), subject if any, **full Markdown**, then attachments (`DownloadableItem` rows + “Bijlagen” label).

### Wiring & docs
- New props/types on **`PortalEmailThreadWindow`**: `onOpenMessageDetail`, `messageBodyPreviewMaxRem`, exported type **`PortalEmailThreadMessageDetailOpen`** ([`portal-email-thread-types.ts`](packages/ui-lib/src/components/portal-chat/portal-email-thread-types.ts)).
- Storybook story **`BodyPreviewAndDetailCta`** uses **`fn()`** from `@storybook/test` for the stacked-panel callback demo.

**Note:** In Storybook/the design system alone, wiring `onOpenMessageDetail` still only invokes the spy; the stacked panel UX is exercised in PT1 alongside `PanelsLayout`.

**Panels note:** Serialized URL props remain `{ suite, scenario, messageId }`. If you deep-link straight to message detail **without** the conversation panel having run first, optimistic-only rows may fall back away from the mock list until the dossier conversation panel has published the live thread once.
